title: Sell Mineral Rights in Southview, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Southview, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Southview in Washington County? We buy Marcellus interests directly, explain deductions honestly, and pay cash.
heroLead: Southview sits right outside Canonsburg, in the thick of the busiest gas development corridor in the whole state, and most families here got their first lease offer before they'd ever heard the words horizontal well.
intro: Southview is an unincorporated community near Canonsburg in Washington County, right in the middle of the wet-gas Marcellus core that Range Resources helped pioneer starting back in 2004. Development here has been steady and dense for close to two decades, which means most tracts around Southview have long since been pooled into producing units, whether the surface itself was ever disturbed by a well pad or not.

That long history is generally good news for value, since we're working with real production numbers instead of speculation. But it also means a lot of Southview leases carry older, less favorable post-production deduction terms that families haven't revisited since they were first signed.

sections.heading: Nearly Two Decades of Development Around Southview
paragraphs: This corner of Washington County was ground zero for the Marcellus wet-gas boom, and it's stayed active far longer than most people outside the industry would expect. Infill wells, refracturing, and new units continue getting permitted here well after the initial rush ended, which keeps a lot of older interests producing steadily rather than declining toward nothing.

sections.heading: Why Early Leases Often Cost Owners the Most
paragraphs: Leases signed in this area during 2004 through 2008 predate a lot of the legal clarity that came later, including the Kilmer v. Elexco decision on post-production deductions. If your family's lease is from that early wave, there's a good chance gathering and compression costs are being deducted before your one-eighth minimum royalty gets calculated, and that gap adds up over years of production.

faqs.question: My family's lease near Southview is nearly twenty years old. Does it still matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially the post-production deduction language, which directly affects your current royalty checks. We review older leases carefully as part of evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: Is development still happening in this area, or has it slowed down?
faqs.answer: Development around Southview has continued steadily for years through infill wells and new units, unlike some counties where activity dropped off sharply after the initial boom.

faqs.question: Can you buy just part of my interest and let me keep the rest?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly structure partial sales so families can access cash now while retaining a piece of the interest long term.

faqs.question: Does infill drilling on my unit change what my interest is worth?
faqs.answer: It can. A second or third round of drilling on an established pad often means continued or renewed production, which we factor into the offer using actual volumes rather than a projection.
